options.text: The area is $10\times 7=70\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ using side $AD$ as the height.
The area is $10\times 4=40\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ using base $AB$ and its corresponding perpendicular height.
The area is $7\times 4=28\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ using $AD$ as base without its own corresponding height.
The area equals $10\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ because $10$ is the base length given.

stem:
Sana's parallelogram $ABCD$ has base $AB=10\,\mathrm{cm}$ and corresponding perpendicular height $4\,\mathrm{cm}$. Side $AD$ measures $7\,\mathrm{cm}$.

Which claim correctly finds the area?

teacher.key_rationale: Area is base times corresponding perpendicular height: 10×4=40. Side AD is not the height to AB.
